questions.text: For a mechanical-ventilation LEA item, what checked local source should control the minimum fresh-air value?

options.text: The DOE fresh-air supply table for the listed occupancy.
A generic room-comfort rule with no occupancy table.
A kitchen hood formula even when the room is an office.
A product catalog airflow value.

questions.rationale: The DOE guidelines list fresh-air supply values by occupancy in Table 6.8, so the occupancy table controls the source-safe answer.
questions.explanation: Equal distribution does not account for the pressure differential principle that makes cross-ventilation effective. Reversed ratios (larger on leeward) contradicts wind pressure physics and reduces ventilation effectiveness. Single-sided ventilation does not achieve cross-ventilation and limits air exchange. Cross-ventilation design typically allocates 5-7% of floor area on the windward (high pressure) side and 3-5% on the leeward (low pressure) side to leverage pressure differentials created by wind-driven ventilation. Asymmetric sizing optimizes air velocity through the space. Cross-Ventilation Design: Windward 5-7%, Leeward 3-5% of floor area

questions.text: When natural ventilation requirements cannot be met, what source-safe substitute path is described in the checked DOE family?

options.text: Use mechanical ventilation and the specified fresh-air rates.
Ignore ventilation if windows are aesthetically difficult.
Use only recirculated air for every occupancy.
Apply a kitchen hood exhaust formula to all rooms.

questions.rationale: The DOE guidelines state that mechanical ventilation may be allowed as a substitute when natural lighting and ventilation requirements cannot be met, with fresh-air supply taken from the specified table.
questions.explanation: 15-20% underestimates the benefit of 18 hours daily natural operation. 22-28% is the realistic annual average accounting for system inefficiencies. 30-40% matches the theoretical maximum cited in Philippine Energy Code for ideal conditions. 42-50% exceeds physical limits and practical system performance. Natural ventilation for 18/24 hours = 75% of operation time; mechanical for 6/24 hours = 25%. If natural saves 45% during operation: 0.75 × 45% = 33.75% of daily energy. Accounting for partial-load efficiency and system controls, annual savings typically achieve 22-28%, lower than theoretical due to part-load performance and seasonal variation. Mixed-Mode Savings: 22-28% annual (realistic); theoretical maximum 30-40% (ideal conditions)
questions.code_citation: Philippine Energy Code 2015; Article section: Mixed-Mode Ventilation

questions.text: In the checked DOE cross-ventilation formula, what variables matter for source-safe exam reasoning?

options.text: Design wind speed, opening effectiveness, and opening area.
Paint finish, room color, and ceiling pattern.
Occupant age, furniture cost, and door hardware.
Only the building height, regardless of openings.

questions.rationale: The DOE cross-ventilation equation relates ventilation rate to design wind speed, opening effectiveness, and opening area.
questions.explanation: 100 µg/m³ is too restrictive and not the ASHRAE standard. 150 µg/m³ is lower than the ASHRAE threshold; paints and adhesives alone do not address total VOCs. 300 µg/m³ exceeds ASHRAE limits; standard materials do not meet IAQ requirements. ASHRAE 62.1 specifies a maximum total VOC concentration of 200 µg/m³. Low-VOC materials, adhesives, and finishes can reduce emissions by 50-70%, particularly during the commissioning phase when natural ventilation at 6-8 ACH accelerates off-gassing. ASHRAE 62.1 VOC Limit: 200 µg/m³ total; low-VOC materials reduce emissions by 50-70%
questions.code_citation: ASHRAE 62.1-2022; Article section: Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs)

questions.text: Under the checked DOE fresh-air table, which listed space has the higher air-change value?

options.text: Commercial, institutional, and industrial kitchen.
Office.
Shop.
Restaurant dining area.

questions.rationale: The DOE fresh-air table lists kitchens at 20 air changes per hour, while offices, restaurants, shops, supermarkets, and department stores are listed at 6 air changes per hour.

questions.text: What caution does the checked DOE fresh-air table add about exceeding listed ventilation rates?

options.text: Do not exceed the listed rate by more than 30 percent unless exceptional circumstances justify it.
Always double every table value.
Always reduce every table value by half.
Ignore table values once mechanical equipment is used.

questions.rationale: The DOE table note says the ventilation rate should not exceed the listed values by more than 30 percent unless exceptional circumstances justify it.
